blocks.text: 过去几个月里，前沿模型在发现漏洞方面的能力大幅提升。我们依然乐观地认为，这将帮助防御方以前所未有的速度发现并修复漏洞。不过，AI 进步的速度已经改变了我们对自身披露实践的看法。

blocks.text: 我们正在缩短协同漏洞披露（CVD）政策中的披露窗口：高危和严重问题从 90 天缩短至 30 天，其他所有问题缩短至 45 天。新的时限适用于 2027 年 1 月 1 日及之后报告给厂商和维护者的漏洞。截至该日期仍在处理中的报告，仍按原有截止日期执行。

中的披露窗口：高危和严重问题从 90 天缩短至 30 天，其他所有问题缩短至 45 天。新的时限适用于 2027 年 1 月 1 日及之后报告给厂商和维护者的漏洞。截至该日期仍在处理中的报告，仍按原有截止日期执行。

blocks.text: 除了缩短披露窗口，我们还做了两项相关调整。第一，如果维护者未回应我们的初始漏洞报告，我们将在 15 天后升级至外部漏洞协调方，而不是原来的 30 天。第二，补丁发布后，我们将在 30 天后分享完整技术细节，而不是原来的 45 天。政策的其余部分保持不变。

blocks.text: 最后，有些高危和严重漏洞是我们 90 多天前报告的，如今已超出当前 CVD 政策的截止期限，却仍未公开披露。我们正在通知这些项目的维护者，将额外给他们 30 天，之后我们将按照更新后的政策，从 2027 年 1 月 1 日起在仪表盘上发布这些报告。

blocks.text: 应对 AI 驱动的漏洞发现

inlines.text: 应对 AI 驱动的漏洞发现

blocks.text: 许多协同披露规范，包括我们自家政策中的规范，都是在 AI 能够发现漏洞之前很久就制定的。这些政策假定修复以人类的速度推进，且同一个漏洞不太可能被独立地再次发现。如今这两个假设都不成立了。模型现在能帮助开发修复方案，而一个模型能发现的漏洞，越来越可能被另一个模型也发现。随着这些能力提升，我们正看到漏洞被重复发现的比率上升。当漏洞有望保密数月时，90 天的窗口是合理的。我们不再认为它能做到这一点，这些调整旨在跟上 AI 能力的进步，并为防御方取得恰当的平衡。

inlines.text: 许多协同披露规范，包括我们自家政策中的规范，都是在 AI 能够发现漏洞之前很久就制定的。这些政策假定修复以人类的速度推进，且同一个漏洞不太可能被独立地再次发现。如今这两个假设都不成立了。模型现在能帮助开发修复方案，而一个模型能发现的漏洞，越来越可能被另一个模型也发现。随着这些能力提升，我们正看到漏洞被重复发现的比率上升。当漏洞有望保密数月时，90 天的窗口是合理的。我们不再认为它能做到这一点，这些调整旨在跟上 AI 能力的进步，并为防御方取得恰当的平衡。

blocks.text: 有些漏洞仍然无法快速修复。难以部署的软件（如关键基础设施）中的缺陷，以及需要修改规范或 RFC 的缺陷，并不总能在 30 天或 45 天内解决。在这些情况下，我们将与厂商共同商定修复时间表。对于任何正被积极利用的漏洞，我们 7 天的披露窗口保持不变。本次政策更新不适用于尚未经过人工审核的 AI 发现结果，例如由 OSS Scanner 发现的问题。

OSS Scanner
发现的问题。

blocks.text: 我们认识到，更短的时限可能给软件维护者带来更大压力。为减轻这一负担，我们将继续在每份报告中附上可操作的指引，并在可能时附上补丁或缓解措施，以最大程度帮助维护者确认发现并修复漏洞。在向单个项目发送大量发现之前，我们也会继续与维护者商定可持续的节奏。

blocks.text: 我们推出了一系列计划，帮助维护者和防御者适应这种新的节奏。关键开源项目的维护者可以申请 OSS Scanner，这是一项免费服务，会用我们最强的模型定期扫描他们的代码，并直接把发现的问题发送给他们。符合条件的维护者和贡献者可以申请 Claude for Open Source Program，免费获得六个月的 Claude Ultra。安全专业人士（包括开源维护者）可以申请我们的 Cyber Verification Program，该计划会针对合法的防御工作调整 Claude 的安全防护措施。

blocks.text: Over the last several months, frontier models have become much better at discovering vulnerabilities. We remain optimistic that this will help defenders find and fix vulnerabilities faster than ever before. However, the speed at which AI is improving has changed how we think about our own disclosure practices.

inlines.text: Over the last several months, frontier models have become much better at
discovering vulnerabilities

. We remain optimistic that this will help defenders find and fix vulnerabilities faster than ever before. However, the speed at which AI is improving has changed how we think about our own disclosure practices.

blocks.text: We’re shortening the disclosure window in our coordinated vulnerability disclosure (CVD) policy from 90 days to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, and to 45 days for all other issues. The new timelines apply to vulnerabilities reported to vendors and maintainers on or after January 1, 2027. In-progress reports as of that date will keep their existing deadlines.

inlines.text: We’re shortening the disclosure window in our
coordinated vulnerability disclosure (CVD) policy

from 90 days to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, and to 45 days for all other issues. The new timelines apply to vulnerabilities reported to vendors and maintainers on or after January 1, 2027. In-progress reports as of that date will keep their existing deadlines.

blocks.text: In addition to shortening the disclosure window, we are making two related changes. First, we will aim to escalate to an external vulnerability coordinator after 15 days instead of 30 if a maintainer does not respond to our initial vulnerability report. Second, we will wait 30 days instead of 45 after a patch is available before sharing full technical details. The rest of our policy remains the same.

inlines.text: In addition to shortening the disclosure window, we are making two related changes. First, we will aim to escalate to an external vulnerability coordinator after 15 days instead of 30 if a maintainer does not respond to our initial vulnerability report. Second, we will wait 30 days instead of 45 after a patch is available before sharing full technical details. The rest of our policy remains the same.

blocks.text: Finally, there are high- and critical-severity vulnerabilities that we reported over 90 days ago and that now exceed the deadline in our current CVD policy that have not yet been disclosed publicly. We are now notifying the maintainers of these projects that we are providing them an additional 30 days, after which time we will publish these reports on our dashboard in line with our updated policy starting January 1, 2027.

Responding to AI-enabled vulnerability discovery

blocks.text: Many coordinated disclosure norms, including those found in our own policy, were developed well before AI could discover vulnerabilities. These policies assumed that fixes moved at human speed and that independent rediscovery of the same bug was unlikely. Neither assumption holds today. Models can now help develop fixes, and a bug that one model can find is increasingly likely to be found by another. We are seeing a higher rate of vulnerability rediscovery as these capabilities increase. A 90-day window made sense when a vulnerability could be expected to stay private for months. We no longer believe it can, and these changes are intended to keep pace with progress in AI capabilities and strike the right balance for defenders.

These policies assumed that fixes moved at human speed and that independent rediscovery of the same bug was unlikely. Neither assumption holds today. Models can now help develop fixes, and a bug that one model can find is increasingly likely to be found by another. We are seeing a higher rate of vulnerability rediscovery as these capabilities increase. A 90-day window made sense when a vulnerability could be expected to stay private for months. We no longer believe it can, and these changes are intended to keep pace with progress in AI capabilities and strike the right balance for defenders.

blocks.text: Some vulnerabilities still can’t be fixed quickly. Flaws in hard-to-deploy software, such as critical infrastructure, and flaws that require changes to a specification or RFC can’t always be resolved in 30 or 45 days. In these cases, we will work with the vendor on a remediation timeline. Our seven-day disclosure window for any vulnerability under active exploitation remains unchanged. This new policy update will not apply to AI-discovered findings that have not received human review, such as those found by OSS Scanner.

blocks.text: We recognize that shorter timelines may put more pressure on software maintainers. To reduce that burden, we will continue to include actionable guidance with each report, along with a patch or mitigation where possible, to best enable the maintainer to confirm a finding and fix the vulnerability. We will also continue to agree on a sustainable pace with maintainers before sending a large volume of findings to a single project.

blocks.text: We offer programs to help maintainers and defenders work at this new pace. Maintainers of critical open-source projects can apply to OSS Scanner, a no-cost service that periodically scans their code with our strongest models and sends them findings directly. Eligible maintainers and contributors can apply to the Claude for Open Source Program for six months of Claude Ultra at no cost. And security professionals, including open-source maintainers, can apply to our Cyber Verification Program, which tailors Claude’s safeguards to enable legitimate defensive work.
